 Judgment
The above writ petition is filed with the following prayers:

"(i) Declare that the act of the Respondents 3 and 4 at whose instance the shop rooms situated in the property of the Petitioners were demolished is highhanded, illegal and in violation of the fundamental rights of the Petitioners guaranteed under Articles 21 and 300A of the Constitution of India thereby entitling them for compensation under public law.

sentences.text: (ii) Issue a writ in the nature of mandamus or any other appropriate writ, order or direction directing the Respondents 3 and 4 to pay compensation for violation of the fundamental rights of the Petitioners as claimed in Exhibit P8 notice or in the alternative WP(C) NO.7185 OF 2017 at the rate to be fixed by this Honourable Court as compensation under public law.

(iii) Issue a writ in the nature of mandamus any other writ, order or direction directing the Respondents to restore possession of the portion of the property of the Petitioners which has been demolished at the expense of the Respondents 3 and 4.
and (iv) grant such other and further reliefs as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit to grant in the facts and circumstances of the case."
SIC 2.

When this writ petition came up for consideration, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners submitted that, a suit filed by the petitioners as OS No.1699/2017 before the Munsiff Court, Thiruvananthapuram is dismissed.
If that be the case, continuation of this writ petition need not be necessary.
If there is any surviving grievance, the WP(C) NO.7185 OF 2017 petitioners can approach the additional 5th respondent.
With the above observation, this writ petition is closed.
